title: Page Sculptor: Fragmentation-aware page packing and eviction pruning
author: Evelyn Park
commits: b8f3c9a: introduce page_sculptor worker and occupancy bitmap
c2a1d47: add page packing algorithm and in-place memmove helpers
d4e9f33: eviction: add fragmentation score and prune-evict heuristic
a13b2f0: integrate sculptor with scheduler/batcher affinity hints
f7c0b6e: tests and perf harness for long-sequence KV workloads
description:
Motivation:
The KV cache is showing increasing internal fragmentation for workloads with many variable-size keys and time-varying tenant footprints. Fragmentation increases spill frequency and surface tail latency during continuous batching. This PR introduces a low-impact background compaction \"page sculptor\" and an eviction-pruning heuristic to prefer packing and keep hot working sets contiguous, reducing spill pressure and improving p99 latency.

Design/Changes (high level):
- Background Page Sculptor: a cooperative background worker that compacts free holes inside a page by relocating live records into contiguous regions using an occupancy bitmap and in-place memmove helpers. The sculptor runs with a bounded CPU budget and is tenant-aware to avoid impacting busy tenants. It is non-blocking for foreground readers and writers: compaction uses versioned moves and a short CAS window to switch pointers.
- Fragmentation Score: each page now maintains a lightweight fragmentation score (0-100) derived from occupancy runs and average free-region size. The score is exposed to the eviction layer.
- Prune-evict heuristic: eviction now accounts for fragmentation score and expected relocation cost. Pages with high fragmentation are deprioritized for immediate eviction; instead, the sculptor is scheduled for those pages and eviction will target low-fragmentation pages first to reduce future churn.
- Soft spill annotations: when free memory pressure crosses a soft threshold, pages are annotated for preferred spill candidates and the allocator avoids allocating new variable-size entries into highly fragmented pages. This reduces immediate spill-over to disk by preferring cheaper relocation or eviction.
- Scheduler & Batcher integration: continuous-batching path now prefers slices that touch compacted/low-fragmentation pages first, improving cache locality for batched token generation and reducing KV miss latencies.

Benchmarks:
- Long-sequence conversational workload (mixed-size keys): 10-14% increased sustained throughput at p50 token throughput for a 2048-token distribution; p99 end-to-end latency reduced by 12-25% depending on tenant mix.
- Cold-start heavy churn test: 22% reduction in spill-to-disk operations and a 30% reduction in write amplification from spill cycles.
- CPU overhead: sculptor runs with a 3-6% CPU budget on production-like machines; net CPU spend was reclaimed via fewer expensive spill operations.

Testing and stability:
- Added unit tests for sculptor invariants and move/rollback behavior.
- Integration tests for eviction ordering and fragmentation score propagation.
- Perf harness runs on perf-lab with representative tenant mixes; a perf regression flagged during initial run was resolved by limiting sculptor concurrency and adding tenant throttling.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary on low-traffic capacity pools with sculptor disabled by default (feature flag).
2) Enable sculptor in read-heavy tenants and validate decreased spill rates for two weeks.
3) Gradual enablement on high-throughput pools with dynamic CPU budget tuning.
4) Monitor fragmentation, spill counts, p99 latency; automatic rollback if spill increases >10% vs baseline.

Notes & related work:
- Complements earlier allocator improvements (segmented slab work) by addressing intra-page free-space fragmentation rather than coarse-grained slab sizing.
- Related Linear: ENG-1298 (KV fragmentation monitoring), ENG-2114 (scheduler affinity hooks).

- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf runs in perf-lab
- [x] Feature-flag gated and rollout plan
